the study of Shahidiet al (2012), which examined interlanguage in the acquisition of the L2 sound system of the Iban, was not a true representation of the facts and that the study was not well conducted.
interlanguage is a natural phenomenon that occurs in L2 acquisition and it is a process of language learning that is influenced by the L1 sound system.
the acquisition of L1 and L2 sound system is a natural phenomenon that involves both cognitive and linguistic factors.

the study of the speech patterns of L2 speakers of Malay language, particularly Iban native speakers.
the acquisition of L1 and L2 sound system, and the influence of L1 on the acquisition of the L2 sound system.
the acquisition of L1 and L2 sound system, and the role of interference in L2 speech production.

interlanguage does exist in L2 acquisition and it is a natural and inevitable phenomenon.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the acquisition of L1 sound system is not necessarily the same with the acquisition of L3 sound system and that interference and interlanguage are two different concepts which are not necessarily interdependent.
the study of Shahid et al (2013) has not been able to provide any substantial evidence in support of its claims.

The main takeaway from our work is that
interlanguage and L1 interference are not the same and they do not occur simultaneously in the acquisition of L1 or L2.

the acquisition of L1 sound system is not the only factor that determines the acquisition of L3 sound system, but that there are other contributing factors such as the L3 sound system itself as well as the L3 learner’s L1 sound system which also play a role in the L3 acquisition of sound system.
interlanguage and L1 interference are two different concepts that are not mutually exclusive but are rather two different concepts that have to be studied independently and not together.
